items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: He wouldn't play nothing; he'd put his trumpet in his lap and wouldn't play.

ctx.x: Yeah. He wouldn't play nothing; he'd put his trumpet in his lap and wouldn't play. I used to look back at him like I wanted to kill him, you know? So I just walked away from the bandstand and I'd go outside on the street someplace; I would walk around to get myself together.
But that's the only time I disagreed -- he didn't know what to do.
